cells.tense: You're here, with the pen, right now.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: at the bench where skill gets built one repetition at a time
cells.ask: If you want: let one person see what this daily care actually costs you, and let one finished piece stay finished — set it down as done, not as given up. What comes back is care that doesn't wear you out.
cells.core: You're tending your practice the way something living gets tended — showing up, giving it what it needs today, and not more. Two things want your hours and you're keeping both alive without starving either, which is the hard part, and you're doing it. The skill is building because the care is steady, not because you're forcing it.\n\nIf you want more from this: let one person see what the daily care costs you, and let one finished piece stay finished — set it down as done, not as given up. What comes back is care that doesn't wear you out.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending the practice without forcing it, and both demands are still alive.

cells.tense: You're bracing at a day that hasn't come yet.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: at the bench where skill gets built one repetition at a time
cells.ask: Stop long enough to take in what the practice has already grown in you — fully, until it lands as yours and not as a step. Then picture where it goes from there, not from what's still wrong. What comes back is care that doesn't exhaust you.
cells.core: You're hovering over the practice. Every repetition gets checked, every slip gets corrected before it's even landed, and you're braced for a day when it's finally good enough — so today's work never gets to just be today's. The tending has turned into holding on, and the holding is wearing you down faster than the work is.\n\nTry stopping long enough to take in what the practice has already grown in you — all of it, until it lands as yours and not as a step toward something else. Then picture where it goes from there, not from what's still wrong. What comes back is care that doesn't exhaust you.
cells.sheetLine: You're gripping the practice so tightly it can't grow.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: at the bench where skill gets built one repetition at a time
cells.ask: Rather than dragging yourself back to the bench by force, say out loud what you still hope this becomes, and keep hoping it past the evidence — the wanting pulls the practice back. What returns is growth that doesn't have to be forced.
cells.core: There was a practice and you stopped tending it. Somewhere back there it stopped paying off, or two demands pulled at once and one went quiet — and you're still standing at that moment, with the skill sitting unwatered. The capacity didn't leave. The daily care did.\n\nThe way back isn't to drag yourself to the bench and grind. It's to say out loud what you still hope this becomes, and to keep hoping it even when the evidence is thin — the wanting is what pulls the practice back toward you. What returns is growth that doesn't have to be forced.
cells.sheetLine: The skill's still there. The tending stopped.

cells.tense: Pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: at the bench where skill gets built one repetition at a time
cells.ask: Say what you're keeping this practice alive for, out loud, to one person who can see what it asks of you. What comes back is care that doesn't drain you, because you've admitted whose it is.
cells.core: You're already keeping it alive. Every day, quietly, you give the practice what it needs and hold the other demands off just enough — and you call it habit, routine, just what you do. The careful tending is running. The one doing it hasn't signed it.\n\nSay what you're keeping this practice alive for — out loud, to one person who can see what it asks of you. Not to be praised; to have the intention on the record. What comes back is care that doesn't drain you, because you've admitted whose it is.
cells.sheetLine: You're already tending this on purpose. You call it routine.
